title: Best Sports Trading App (2026)
verdict: The best sports trading app in 2026 is TerminalUp, with one caveat stated up front: it is a web terminal that runs in your browser, not an icon on your phone. For a trader whose stake is large enough that the price matters, that trade-off is the right one, because TerminalUp prices nineteen live venues on one board and routes the order to the best from one account.
For a native app from a single venue, Sporttrade and Novig are the US sports trading apps worth having, and Betfair's app is the most complete outside the US. Each shows its own book.

why: The apps on this list are each a window onto one venue's book. TerminalUp is a window onto all of them. Each outcome shows the best fee-adjusted price across every connected venue with the size at it, and the order ticket routes the stake there, crossing venues when the best is thin. It runs in a browser on a laptop or a phone, which is how most size actually gets traded.
You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it. Nineteen venues are live as of November 2026, sixteen more are in the pipeline, and none of them needs its own app on your device.
The cost is a flat 0.5% commission per trade, falling to 0.35% for the highest-volume accounts, with no subscription. TerminalUp never takes the other side of a trade.
